abstract: Gene-environment interaction (G×E) analyses play a crucial role in advancing genetic discovery, addressing missing heritability, and facilitating precision medicine. However, existing G×E methods are mostly designed for cross-sectional data, limiting the utility of longitudinal data. Here we propose SAGELD, a scalable and accurate genome-wide G×E method for longitudinal traits that controls for sample relatedness in large-scale datasets. SAGELD uses matrix projection to construct test statistics and the SPAGRM framework to efficiently control for sample relatedness, achieving 10- to 10,000-fold speedups over existing methods while maintaining greater power than cross-sectional analyses. We evaluated SAGELD through extensive simulations and UK Biobank analyses. Using age and body mass index as environmental exposures, we identified 74 loci with genetic × age interactions and 5 loci with genetic × adiposity interactions in the pooled analysis of longitudinal primary care data and cross-sectional assessment data. These results highlight the advantages of leveraging longitudinal data in G×E analyses.
